items.description: Book the first obstetric visit (weeks 6-8) and start the pregnancy card (karta ciąży)
Confirm the pregnancy: beta-hCG blood test and the first ultrasound with a heartbeat
Baseline blood work: blood group and Rh factor, antibody screen, complete blood count, fasting glucose, urinalysis, TSH
Infection screening: HIV, HCV, HBs antigen, syphilis (VDRL), rubella IgG, toxoplasmosis IgG and IgM, CMV
First-trimester screening: ultrasound with nuchal translucency plus the PAPP-A test (weeks 11-13+6)
Cervical cytology if not done in the last year, and a dental check-up (free during pregnancy in Poland)
Start the supplements agreed with the doctor: folic acid, iodine, vitamin D, DHA
Get the doctor's certificate confirming the pregnancy before week 10 - some employment and benefit rights depend on it
Write down the due date and put the week-by-week milestones in the calendar
Agree who to tell and when; tell the employers once you are both ready
Take over the chores with chemicals, heavy lifting, cat litter and raw meat
Learn the warning signs (bleeding, severe pain, fever, no movement later on) and save the maternity ward's number
Stop smoking in the flat and the car, and keep alcohol out of the household
Review the household budget for a period on one income plus the baby purchases
Check your employer's rules for paternity leave (urlop ojcowski) and parental leave (urlop rodzicielski)
Decide whether a private prenatal care package is worth it, and check what the insurance covers
Start a separate savings buffer for the birth and the first months
Ask about antenatal class (szkoła rodzenia) places - the good ones are booked months ahead
Read one solid book on pregnancy and birth, and agree with your partner what you both want from the birth
Obstetric visit roughly every 4 weeks, with blood pressure and weight tracked each time
Anatomy ultrasound (weeks 18-22)
Oral glucose tolerance test, 75 g (weeks 24-28)
Repeat blood count, urinalysis and antibody screen (weeks 21-26)
Anti-D immunoglobulin around week 28 if the mother is Rh negative - confirm with the doctor
Ask the doctor about the flu and pertussis (Tdap) vaccination for the mother (weeks 27-36)
Dental follow-up before the third trimester
Attend the antenatal class together, breastfeeding and newborn-care sessions included
Book the hospital tour and ask what the delivery room allows the partner to do
Take an infant first-aid and CPR course
Write the birth plan with the midwife and agree your part in it
Choose the hospital and the route; time the drive at night and at rush hour
Plan the baby corner: cot, changing area, storage, blackout curtain, room thermometer
Do any renovation, painting or furniture assembly now, not in the third trimester
Cot or crib with a firm mattress, two fitted sheets and a sleeping bag
Pram with a carrycot, rain cover and mosquito net
Car seat (i-Size or group 0+, rear-facing) with its base - fit it and practise before the birth
Baby carrier or wrap for the first months
Changing mat or table, newborn nappies, wipes and cotton pads, barrier cream
Baby bath, bath thermometer, two soft hooded towels
Clothes in sizes 56 and 62: bodysuits, rompers, hats, socks, scratch mittens, swaddles
Feeding kit: bottles and teats, steriliser, bottle brush, breast pump (buying or renting), nursing bras and pads
Baby monitor, night light, room thermometer with a hygrometer
Baby medicine cabinet: digital thermometer, saline drops, nasal aspirator, nail scissors, sterile gauze, infant paracetamol after the doctor's advice
Tell your employer the paternity leave dates you are planning
Prepare the mother's maternity leave paperwork with her employer or ZUS
Visits every 2-3 weeks, then weekly from week 37, with CTG monitoring from week 38
Group B streptococcus swab (GBS, weeks 35-37)
Repeat blood count, urinalysis, HIV, HCV and HBs antigen (weeks 33-37)
Growth ultrasound (weeks 28-32)
Register at the maternity ward and hand in the documents it asks for
Discuss pain relief with the doctor: what the ward offers and whether an epidural is available
Fit the car seat in the actual car and practise the straps with a doll
Assemble the cot and wash the clothes and bedding at 60 degrees
Fill the freezer with meals for the first two weeks
Deep-clean the flat and set up the changing corner with everything within one arm's reach
Agree the 'it is starting' plan: who drives, who has the keys, who takes the pet, and the backup driver
Save the numbers: ward, midwife, taxi, family, your own workplace
Agree with the family how visits after the birth will work, and that they come to help rather than be hosted
Keep the car fuelled above half and the power bank charged from week 36
Choose the community midwife (położna środowiskowa) who will visit after the birth
Mother's documents: ID card, pregnancy card, test results, ward registration papers, a copy of the birth plan
Mother's clothes: two nursing nightgowns, dressing gown, slippers, shower flip-flops, warm socks
Postpartum pads, disposable underwear, nursing bra and breast pads
Mother's toiletries, two towels, hairband, lip balm
Water bottle with a straw, snacks and isotonic drinks for the labour
Phone charger with a long cable and a power bank
Baby clothes: bodysuits and rompers in sizes 56 and 62, two hats, socks, scratch mittens, swaddle or blanket
Newborn nappies, wipes or cotton pads, baby cream
Going-home outfit for the baby, and the car seat left ready in the car
Father's bag: ID card, cash and cards, parking money or app, comfortable clothes, food and drinks
Camera or phone with free storage, and the list of people to inform
Cord blood banking kit, if you decided on it
Put the packed bag by the door and tell your partner exactly where it is
Call the ward before leaving, take the bag, the documents and the car seat
Time the contractions and note when the waters broke and what they looked like
At admission: hand over the documents and ask about rooming-in and what the partner may do
During labour: drinks, massage, pacing the breathing, and speaking for the birth plan when she cannot
Ask for skin-to-skin contact and the first feed within the first hour if the condition of both allows
Have the midwife show you a nappy change, swaddling, bathing, burping and umbilical cord care
Confirm the consent forms: vitamin K, hepatitis B and BCG vaccination
Check that the newborn screening test and the hearing screening are done before discharge
Ask the ward to report the birth to the registry office, and collect the discharge summary, the vaccination card and the child's health book
Arrange food, a shower and a few hours of sleep for yourself - the first days are long
Register the birth at the registry office (USC) within 21 days and collect several copies of the birth certificate (odpis aktu urodzenia)
Check that the child has a PESEL number and register the address (meldunek)
Apply for the one-off birth grant (becikowe) within 12 months, if your income qualifies
Apply for the 800+ child benefit (świadczenie wychowawcze) through ZUS in the month of the birth
Add the child to health insurance through your employer
File for paternity leave (urlop ojcowski): 2 weeks, to be used within 12 months of the birth
Register the child with a primary care clinic (POZ) and choose the paediatrician
Review life insurance, beneficiaries and the will now that there is a dependant
Community midwife visits (wizyty patronażowe) - at least four in the first six weeks
Postpartum check-up for the mother around week 6
Watch for signs of postpartum depression in her and in yourself, and keep the helpline number handy
Support breastfeeding: check the latch, and have a lactation consultant's number ready before you need it
First paediatric visit and the vaccinations due in the first weeks
Track feeds, nappies and weight until the paediatrician says it is no longer needed
Safe sleep every time: on the back, own flat surface, no pillow or bumpers, room at 18-21 degrees
Take a fixed share of the nights, the cooking and the cleaning - agreed in advance, not improvised
Keep visits short and give every visitor a job
Sleep in shifts so each of you gets one unbroken block
Stock up on what runs out fastest: nappies, wipes, pads, food you can eat with one hand
Keep to the vaccination calendar (kalendarz szczepień): visits around months 2, 3-4, 5-6, 7 and 12-13
Well-baby check-ups and developmental screening with the paediatrician
Baby-proof the flat around month 6: socket covers, corner guards, stair gate, cupboard locks, window locks, furniture anchored to the wall
Check the car seat's height and weight limits and move up a size when the child outgrows it
Start solids around month 6: high chair, bibs, soft spoons, plates
Bigger clothes, sleeping bag in the next size, and shoes only once the child walks
Plan and split the parental leave (urlop rodzicielski), including the 9 weeks reserved for the father
Apply for a nursery place (żłobek) early - the waiting lists are long
Get the child's ID document if you plan to travel abroad
Review the budget and start a long-term savings account for the child
Keep one evening a month for the two of you, and ask for help to make it happen
Practise before the birth: nappy change, bottle preparation, burping and bathing on a doll
Learn the safe sleep rules and the shaken-baby warning, and make sure everyone who will care for the baby knows them
Save the emergency numbers in your phone and in hers
Agree in advance: nights, visitors, feeding approach, sleeping arrangements, screen time, and what you will not compromise on
Talk about your own fears and expectations instead of waiting for them to surface at 3 a.m.
Find other fathers to talk to - a group, a friend, anyone one year ahead of you
Look after your own sleep, food and exercise; you cannot support anyone while empty
Sort out work: handover notes, calendar blocked for the leave, and an out-of-office plan that holds
